item.title: Dengue: 3 deaths, 1,097 cases reported in 24 hours
item.description:
Health officials on Sunday said they recorded 1,097 fresh cases of dengue, with at least three people dying from the disease in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, (of the 1,097) 123 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 116 in Chittagong division, 258 in Dhaka division, 109 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 82 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 243 in Khulna division, 81 in Mymensingh division, 76 in Rajshahi division, six in Rangpur division and three in Sylhet division,” a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the dengue outbreak began in Bangladesh this year, the disease has so far claimed 93 lives and infected 34,783 people.
Dengue claimed 413 lives and infected 102,861 people in the country last year.
Besides, dengue claimed 575 lives and infected 101,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Nepal begins burials as flood death toll rises to 752
item.description:
Nepal said Sunday it had begun burying some of the hundreds of bodies recovered after devastating floods after taking DNA samples and marking them so families can later retrieve them.
The dead are traditionally cremated on funeral pyres in Hindu-majority Nepal, so the burials are viewed as long-term storage until families can retrieve them.
Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told reporters that all those buried were carefully recorded but also appealed for international support, saying Nepal needed “more than a thousand” freezer units to store bodies.
The announcement of the burials came as Nepal’s disaster ministry increased its toll again on Sunday to 752 bodies recovered and 2,502 people missing.
That list includes 589 foreigners unaccounted for.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 dead in Tibet and 546 people missing following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the overall toll to 768 dead and 3,048 unaccounted for.
“Following standard and accepted protocols, such as those of ICRC (Red Cross), the mortal remains of the dead, especially those not recognizable... have been temporarily buried,” Rai told reporters.
“Medical teams took DNA samples from every victim prior to the burial so that families can match-reference later and would be allowed to exhume for necessary rituals.”
Nepal has called for freezer storage units and DNA testing kits, as it is overwhelmed with the number of bodies to store safely.
“We have requested different countries for freezers; we will need more than a thousand,” Rai added.
“Many dead bodies have been collected, and they have started decomposing. To preserve public health, we had to bury the decomposing bodies,” he added.

item.title: Mirza Abbas to return home Sept 2 after treatment
item.description:
BNP Standing Committee Member and Prime Minister’s Adviser Mirza Abbas will return home on September 2 following treatment in Singapore and Malaysia for a prolonged period.
Confirming the matter on Sunday, BNP Media Cell member Shayrul Kabir Khan said Mirza Abbas is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka at 9pm on September 2 on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight.
He said Mirza Abbas, after receiving treatment in Singapore and Malaysia for a long time as advised by a medical board, has recovered considerably by the grace of Allah, and is returning home from Malaysia.
Mirza Abbas was admitted to Prince Court Medical Centre in Malaysia on April 14 for physiotherapy.
Earlier, on March 11, he suddenly fell unconscious during iftar and was admitted to Evercare Hospital Dhaka.
A medical team performed emergency brain surgery on him. Following the operation, he was flown to Singapore General Hospital by an air ambulance on March 15 for better treatment.
After nearly a month of intensive care in Singapore, doctors advised physiotherapy, leading to his admission at the specialised Prince Court Medical Centre in Malaysia.

item.title: DBL Ceramics’ TileChalk wins SDG Grand Prix at MAD Stars 2026
item.description:
DBL Ceramics’ sustainability initiative TileChalk has won the Grand Prix in the SDGs category at MAD Stars 2026, alongside two Crystal Awards in PR and Brand Experience & Activation, marking another significant international milestone for the initiative from Bangladesh.
TileChalk addresses a challenge within ceramic manufacturing by transforming ceramic sludge generated during the production process into classroom chalk.
The initiative turns an industrial by-product into a useful resource, bringing together waste reduction, circularity, education and community impact.
The three MAD Stars recognitions add to TileChalk’s growing international track record.
The initiative has previously received awards and recognition at ADFEST, The One Show, AdForum PHNX Awards and Spikes Asia.
The project’s journey has also demonstrated that sustainability can extend beyond the factory floor.
By developing a practical use for ceramic waste and making the process open source, TileChalk seeks to encourage wider adoption of the idea and demonstrate how manufacturing waste can be reimagined as a resource.
Commenting on the achievement, Mohammad Bayazed Bashar, chief business officer of DBL Ceramics, said: “We are grateful for every recognition TileChalk has received and these three awards at MAD Stars are an important milestone for us. But we believe recognition should encourage us to move forward, not stop here. There is still much more we can do to reduce waste and lessen our environmental impact. TileChalk has shown us that meaningful solutions can come from looking differently at the challenges within our own industry. Our responsibility now is to keep innovating, keep learning and continue working towards a more sustainable future.”
With its latest achievement at MAD Stars, TileChalk, the initiative developed by DBL Ceramics in collaboration with POP5, continues to demonstrate how a locally developed solution can address a global sustainability challenge, while reinforcing DBL Ceramics’ commitment to responsible manufacturing and environmental innovation.

item.title: NCC Bank aids those injured during July 2024 uprising
item.description:
As part of its CSR initiatives, NCC Bank has provided a one-time grant of Tk1.5 crore to the Aparajito 24 Foundation to support the medical treatment and economic self-reliance of individuals severely injured during the July 2024 uprising.
Through this assistance, 50 people who were critically affected by the July 24 uprising will be brought under rehabilitation programs.
Each beneficiary will receive support of up to Tk3 lakh.
The fund will be utilized for a combination of medical treatment and equipment, coordination for employment opportunities, provision of materials for income-generating activities, supervision of tree plantation initiatives, and direct financial assistance, as required.
The primary objective is to rehabilitate the affected individuals and make them self-sufficient by creating sustainable income opportunities.
Recently, at an event organized at NCC Bank's head office, NCC Bank chairman Md Nurun Newaz Salim handed over a check for Tk1.5 crore to Saiful Islam, vice president of Aparajito 24 Foundation.
Present on the occasion were NCC Bank vice chairman Engr Abdus Salam, managing director M Shamsul Arefin, and company secretary (current charge) Md Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, along with Aparajito 24 Foundation's general secretary Dr M Mustajib Haider, Shahriar Akter Haque, program coordinator Abdullah As Sakib, and program officer Tasmia Hoque Mowsomi.
Aparajito 24 Foundation is a voluntary, non-profit, and non-political organization.
The foundation is working with various institutions, including the July Shaheed Smriti Foundation, Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (Blast), Drik, Vision Eye Hospital, Combined Military Hospital (CMH), and the Vocational Training Center for the Blind, to rebuild the lives of affected individuals and their families.
NCC Bank chairman Md Nurun Newaz Salim said: "Many of those affected during the July 2024 uprising are still facing challenges in their lives and livelihoods. Our goal with this assistance is to help them achieve economic self-reliance and rebuild their lives with dignity."
NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin said: "The primary goal of our social responsibility initiatives is to bring about long-term, sustainable, and meaningful social change. This assistance provided through Aparajito 24 Foundation will play an effective role in making the critically injured of the July 2024 movement financially self-reliant. However, this is not merely a symbolic check handover; rather, it is a small yet sincere step driven by our sense of duty—an effort to express our deep gratitude and unwavering solidarity to those who have drenched the dream of a discrimination-free society and justice for all with their own blood."

item.title: Three family members perform at Jaltaranga's cultural evening
item.description:
Jaltaranga, a Dhaka-based cultural organization, organized a musical evening titled “Coffee House-er Adday" at the Ishfendiyar Zahed Hasan Auditorium of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro in Dhaka on August 28, 2026.
Three members of one family performed at the event: Zakir Hossain Tapan; his wife, Tanvira Ashraf Shyama; and their son,Shahrivar Hossain, also known as Rivu. Hossain accompanied his parents on guitar.
The program opened with a group rendition of Kazi Nazrul Islam's "Joy Hok Joy Hok" and Rabindranath Tagore's "Alokero Ei Jhornadharay."
The artists then performed a selection of songs from earlier decades of Bengali music, including "Joy Hok Joy Hok Shantir Joy Hok," "Keno Dure Thako Shudhu," "Shono Kono Ekdin," "O Mor Moyna Go," "Ogo Mor Modhumita," "Mone Pore Ruby Roy," "O Keno Eto Sundori Holo," and "Coffee House-er Sei Adda-ta Aaj Aar Nei."
The main program began at 7pm, with the auditorium filled to capacity. Audience members said such programs were necessary to keep the tradition alive and called for similar events to be held regularly.
Tapan said, "Jaltaranga is always committed to introducing the golden era of Bengali music to new listeners."

item.title: Ex-IGP Enamul Huq passes away
item.description:
Former Inspector General of Police (IGP) M Enamul Huq passed away at a hospital in the capital on Sunday. He was 88.
He breathed his last in the early hours, according to a press release issued by Police Headquarters.
Enamul is survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter.
A namaz-e-janaza for him was held after Zohr prayers at the SI Shiru Miah Auditorium in the Rajarbagh Police Lines, followed by an official state funeral.
He will be laid to rest at his family graveyard in Godagari upazila of Rajshahi district.
Additional Inspector General (AIG) AKM Awlad Hossain laid a wreath at the coffin on behalf of IGP Md Ali Hossain Fakir. Tributes were also paid on behalf of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), Bangladesh Police Service Association and the Retired Police Officers' Welfare Association.
Enamul served as IGP from October 16, 1991 to July 8, 1992.
During his distinguished career, he also served as the DMP commissioner, the principal of the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sarda, Rajshahi and a member of the Law Commission of Bangladesh.
Enamul was the only elected member of Interpol from Bangladesh from 1988 to 1992. He also worked with various United Nations agencies.
He was also an accomplished writer who authored approximately 14 books and regularly wrote columns for national and international publications.
Meanwhile, IGP Ali Hossain and the Bangladesh Police Service Association expressed deep shock at the death of the former IGP.

Questions over arrest of 2 suspects and colour of recovered motorbike
item.description:
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has announced the arrest of two suspects, including the prime suspect, in connection with the death of 56-year-old headteacher Ranjila Parveen.

Ranjila Parveen tragically lost her life after falling from a battery-powered auto-rickshaw when muggers violently snatched her bag in front of the Jatiya Sangsad (national parliament) building. RAB also reported the recovery of the motorcycle allegedly used during the crime.

The arrestees have been identified as Mosharaf Hossain Poni (alias Poni Gazi) and his accomplice, Sedric. RAB stated that they seized a Yamaha R15 motorcycle from the two, which they believe was used in the mugging.

The details were disclosed during a press briefing held at 4:00 pm today (Sunday) at the RAB-2 Battalion Headquarters in Basila, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. Additional Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Naimul Hassan, Commanding Officer of RAB-2, led the briefing.

Following the briefing, the prime suspect and his associate were presented before journalists. At that point, Mosharaf Hossain shouted out, protesting his innocence and claiming he had no involvement in the incident. He further asserted that his motorcycle bore no resemblance to the one used in the mugging.

Meanwhile, CCTV footage from two separate cameras circulated on Saturday showed a blue motorcycle at the scene, raising doubts regarding the identity of the arrested suspects and the colour of the seized vehicle.

Addressing the arrests, RAB officer Naimul Hassan stated that, based on intelligence and technological analysis, prime suspect Mosharaf Hossain and his accomplice Sedric were apprehended in the Purba Tejturi Bazar area of the capital. The Yamaha R15 motorcycle used in the crime was also recovered. THe officers were able to track down the suspects within 24 hours of the fatality, he added.

Naimul Hassan explained that the seized motorcycle belongs to an individual named Rakib, who has been detained for questioning. However, on the day of the incident, the motorcycle was in Poni Gazi’s possession. Furthermore, RAB claimed that the victim’s husband, Abdul Matin, confirmed that a vehicle matching this description was used at the crime scene.

The RAB official added that initial investigations reveal Poni Gazi to be a professional mugger with a history of multiple crimes. He had been operating in areas such as Tejgaon and Sher-e-Bangla Nagar for a prolonged period, engaging in robbery, mugging, drug dealing, and intimidation. He currently faces 13 cases across various police stations in and outside the capital.

Providing a breakdown of the charges, Naimul Hassan noted that Poni Gazi has three drug-related cases registered at Hatirjheel, Adabor, and Kafrul police stations; six cases involving theft and criminal intimidation at Bhatara, Mohammadpur, Kafrul, Badda, and Shahjahanpur stations; and three cases of theft and burglary at Adabor, Khilgaon, and Kamrangirchar stations. Additionally, he faces a case for preparing to commit dacoity at Chandpur Model police station.

The RAB-2 commander further mentioned that Poni Gazi had previously been arrested by law enforcement authorities and subsequently released on bail, though the exact date of his release is still being verified by the police.

While specific details regarding Sedric remain limited at this stage, the motorcycle owner confirmed that Sedric was riding pillion behind Poni, he added.

RAB’s 3 major arguments

In response to journalists' queries, RAB-2 Commanding Officer Naimul Hassan presented three main arguments justifying the arrests:

Firstly, the motorcycle's owner, Rakib, stated in his testimony that Poni Gazi frequently took the bike by force. It remained in Poni’s possession from 26 August until Saturday afternoon, and Rakib claimed to be unaware of what Poni did with it during that period.

Secondly, the physical build of the rider seen in the CCTV footage matches that of Poni. Furthermore, 15 local informants confirmed Poni’s involvement after reviewing the video. The recovered motorcycle was also shown to the deceased teacher’s husband, who confirmed that an identical motorcycle was used in the crime.

Thirdly, mobile phone tracking placed the suspects' numbers in the vicinity of the crime scene between 2:30 am and 4:00 am.

Speaking regarding the relationship between the owner, Rakib, and Poni Gazi, Naimul Hassan explained that Poni is a senior figure from Rakib's neighbourhood. Rakib, who works in an auto repair workshop, was regularly threatened and coerced into lending his motorcycle. Rakib remains in custody for questioning to determine the extent of his involvement; if complicity is proven, he will be formally arrested, though no decision has been taken yet.

Question about motorbike colour

At the conclusion of the briefing, the two suspects were presented before media cameras in the courtyard of the RAB-2 headquarters, escorted by four RAB officers.

As they were brought out, Poni Gazi shouted to newspersons, maintaining that he was innocent and had been detained unlawfully.

He pointed out that his motorcycle is black and white, whereas the vehicle captured in the mugging footage was blue, urging journalists to investigate the discrepancy independently. RAB personnel swiftly escorted him away immediately after.

Media outlets had earlier broadcast CCTV footage showing two suspects on a blue motorcycle loitering on the road in front of the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad.

In contrast, photographs of the recovered motorcycle provided to the media by RAB clearly show a black-and-white vehicle. This stark variance has fueled growing scepticism over whether the seized bike and the arrested individuals were genuinely involved in the crime.

When questioned about this mismatch, Naimul Hassan remarked, "We have consistently stated that they have been arrested as suspects, as the perpetrators named in the case file remain unidentified. The investigation will develop progressively from these initial arrests. We will wait for further clarity before drawing definitive conclusions. The two individuals will shortly be handed over to the police station, after which we will seek court permission to interrogate them."
